the interfacial reaction in Cu/Sn system is a diffusion-controlled process, which is described by the parabolic growth law, and that the interfacially reaction in the Cu-Su system is affected by the processing route of the sample.
the growth of the Cu3Sn phase is significantly influenced by the processing route.

the growth of Cu3Sntakes place in two different regimes: at low temperatures (T < 200 °C) the growth is diffusion controlled and at high temperatures (T > 200 °C), the growth is controlled by interface kinetics.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the diffusion parameters are not the same for different types of samples, but are rather strongly dependent on the sample processing route.
the diffusion growth of Cu3 Sn phase is faster in the bump than in the thin film Cu/Su system.
the diffusion coefficient of Cu in the Cu3Sn phase is significantly higher than the diffusion coefficient of Sn in the Cu3Si phase.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the growth kinetics is controlled by the diffusion of tin in the Cu/Sn thin film structure, whereas it is limited by the diffusion of copper in the bump structure.
the growth of Cu3 Sn intermetallics is much faster in the case of thin film structures than in the bump structure.
the intermetallic growth is faster in thin film Cu/SnPb than in bump Cu/SnAg.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the growth kinetics of intermetallic phases can be controlled by the processing conditions.
the diffusion parameters for the growth of Cu3Sntype intermetallic in the Cu-Sntype interconnects are dependent on the processing route.
the diffusion parameters for Cu-Sn interfacial reaction are strongly dependent on the processing route.
